n: Use 是 to say that A is B. There is no "to be" for adjectives (see the 很 lesson), and the verb never changes form.
Add 吗 to the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. The word order does not change. Answer with the verb: 是, 不是, 有, 没有...
Put 的 between the owner and the thing owned. With close family and friends, 的 is often dropped: 我妈妈, 我朋友.
Put 不 directly before a verb or adjective to negate it. 不 becomes bù→bú before another fourth tone (不是 bú shì). For 有, use 没有 instead.
在 means "to be at". It can be the main verb (我在家) or come before another verb to say where the action happens (我在家吃饭).
A descriptive adjective normally takes a degree word such as 很 before it, with no 是. Here 很 is often weak and simply means "is".
有 means "to have" and also "there is". Its negative is 没有, never 不有.

x.en: Do you have an older brother?

p: Use the question word where the answer goes
n: Chinese question words (什么, 谁, 哪儿, 几, 多少) stay in the same place as the answer in a statement. No word-order change is needed.

x.en: What do you want to eat?

n: After a topic has been introduced, 呢 asks "and what about...?" without repeating the sentence.

x.en: I am a student, and her?

p: Subject + 想 / 会 / 能 + verb
n: 想 (want to), 会 (know how to) and 能 (be able to) go right before the main verb.

p: A 和 B 都 + verb
n: 和 joins nouns ("and"). 都 means "all" and comes before the verb, never before the subject.

x.py: Wǒ hé nǐ dōu shì xuésheng.
x.en: You and I are both students.

n: Between a number (or 这/那) and a noun, Chinese needs a measure word. 个 is the most common one; 本 is used for books.

x.en: How many children do you have?

n: 太...了 means "too / so ...". It is used for strong feelings, good or bad.
了 marks that something has happened or a situation has changed. 我买了书 = I bought books; 下雨了 = It has started raining.

x.py: Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.

n: Put 过 right after a verb to say you have done it at least once in the past. The negative is 没 + verb + 过.

x.py: Tā méi kàn guò zhè gè diànyǐng.
x.en: He has not seen this film.

n: 得 links a verb to a description of how well or how fast it is done. Put the verb first, then 得, then the adjective.
就 shows that something happens soon or quickly. 就要...了 means "about to".

x.py: Nǐ děng yíxià, wǒ jiù lái.
x.en: Wait a moment, I will be right there.

x.py: Tā qī diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
x.en: He got up at seven already.
The film is about to start.

n: 比 puts two things side by side: A 比 B + adjective. Do not add 很 before the adjective. To say "not as ... as", use 没有.

x.py: Zhè gè bǐ nà gè guì.
x.en: This one is more expensive than that one.

n: 因为 gives the reason and 所以 gives the result. Chinese often uses both, where English uses only one.

x.py: Yīnwèi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ wǒ bù qù.
x.en: Because it is raining, I am not going.

x.h: 因为他生病了，所以没来。
x.py: Yīnwèi tā shēngbìng le, suǒyǐ méi lái.
x.en: He was ill, so he did not come.

x.h: 因为我很忙，所以没有时间。
x.py: Yīnwèi wǒ hěn máng, suǒyǐ méiyǒu shíjiān.
x.en: I am busy, so I have no time.

n: 虽然 means "although" and 但是 means "but". Chinese uses both together where English uses only one of them.

x.h: 虽然很累，但是他很高兴。
x.py: Suīrán hěn lèi, dànshì tā hěn gāoxìng.
x.en: Although he is tired, he is happy.

x.py: Suīrán zhè gè guì, dànshì hěn hǎo.
x.en: Although this is expensive, it is good.

x.h: 虽然天气冷，但是我们还是去。
x.py: Suīrán tiānqì lěng, dànshì wǒmen háishì qù.
x.en: Although it is cold, we are going anyway.

n: 还是 offers a choice between two options inside one question. Do not add 吗.

x.py: Nǐ hē chá háishì hē kāfēi?
x.en: Do you drink tea or coffee?
Are you going, or am I?
Is he a teacher or a student?

n: 可以 means "may" or "can" when permission is involved. Use 不可以 (or 不能) to say it is not allowed.
别 before a verb means "don't". It is used for commands and requests. Adding 了 softens it or means "stop".
已经 means "already". It comes before the verb, and 了 usually closes the sentence.

t: Actions in progress with 正在
n: 正在 (or 在) before a verb shows that an action is happening right now. 呢 can be added at the end.

t: From...to... with 从 and 到
n: 从 marks the starting point (place or time) and 到 marks the end point.

x.py: Wǒ cóng jiā zǒu dào xuéxiào.
x.en: I walk from home to school.

x.h: 从星期一到星期五我都工作。
x.py: Cóng xīngqīyī dào xīngqīwǔ wǒ dōu gōngzuò.
x.en: I work from Monday to Friday.

p: A 离 B + 远 / 近
n: 离 means "away from". It tells how far A is from B. 远 means far and 近 means near.

x.py: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào hěn jìn.
x.en: My home is close to school.
The hospital is not far from here.

x.py: Xuéxiào lí nǐ jiā yuǎn ma?
x.en: Is the school far from your home?

t: A little, briefly with 一下
n: 一下 after a verb makes the action short and casual, like "have a go at". It also softens requests.

x.en: I want to rest a bit.

n: 让 means "to let" or "to make". The person after 让 does the next verb.

x.py: Māma bù ràng wǒ hē kāfēi.
x.en: Mom does not let me drink coffee.
The teacher has us write our names.

x.py: Tā ràng wǒ gěi tā dǎdiànhuà.
x.en: He asked me to call him.

t: Doing something for someone with 给
n: 给 before a person shows who receives or benefits from the action. As a verb it also means "to give".

x.py: Tā gěi wǒ yì běn shū.
Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi shuǐ.
x.en: Please give me a glass of water.

n: 如果 means "if". The result clause usually has 就 (or 会) before its verb. 要是 can replace 如果 in speech.

x.h: 如果明天下雨，我就不去。
x.py: Rúguǒ míngtiān xiàyǔ, wǒ jiù bù qù.
x.en: If it rains tomorrow, I won't go.

x.py: Rúguǒ nǐ lèi le, jiù xiūxi ba.
x.en: If you are tired, then rest.

x.h: 如果你有时间，就来我家玩。
x.py: Rúguǒ nǐ yǒu shíjiān, jiù lái wǒ jiā wán.
x.en: If you have time, come to my place.

n: 才 after a time word shows that something happened later, or took more effort, than expected. 就 shows the opposite: early or easy.

x.en: He only gets up at nine.
It is only seven o'clock now.

x.h: 我等了三个小时才看到他。
x.py: Wǒ děng le sān gè xiǎoshí cái kàndào tā.
x.en: I waited three hours before I saw him.

t: Repeating with 又 and 又...又...
p: 又 + verb / 又 A 又 B
n: 又 refers to something that has already happened again. 又 A 又 B joins two qualities: "both A and B".

x.py: Zhè gè cài yòu piányi yòu hǎochī.
x.en: This dish is both cheap and tasty.

x.h: 他昨天来了，今天又来了。
x.py: Tā zuótiān lái le, jīntiān yòu lái le.
x.en: He came yesterday and came again today.
She is both smart and pretty.

n: 更 means "even more". It is often used after 比 to stress a bigger gap.

x.py: Zhè gè bǐ nà gè gèng hǎo.
x.en: This one is even better than that one.
Today is even colder than yesterday.
He is even busier than me.

t: Being the same with 一样
p: A 跟 B 一样 (+ adjective)
n: 跟 (or 和) joins the two things being compared and 一样 means "the same". Add an adjective at the end to say in what way.

x.en: I am as tall as you.

x.py: Zhè gè hé nà gè yíyàng guì.
x.en: This one is as expensive as that one.

x.py: Tā de shū gēn wǒ de yíyàng.
x.en: His book is the same as mine.

t: First...then... with 先 and 然后
n: 先 means "first" and 然后 means "then / after that". Together they put actions in order.

x.en: First wash your hands, then eat.

x.h: 我先写作业，然后看电视。
x.py: Wǒ xiān xiě zuòyè, ránhòu kàn diànshì.
x.en: I do homework first, then watch TV.

x.h: 我们先吃饭，然后去公园。
x.py: Wǒmen xiān chīfàn, ránhòu qù gōngyuán.
x.en: We eat first, then go to the park.

n: 为了 introduces the goal for which an action is done, like "in order to / for the sake of".

x.h: 为了学习汉语，他去了北京。
x.py: Wèile xuéxí hànyǔ, tā qù le Běijīng.
x.en: To learn Chinese, he went to Beijing.
For my health, I run every day.

x.h: 他为了工作搬到了上海。
x.py: Tā wèile gōngzuò bān dào le Shànghǎi.
x.en: He moved to Shanghai for work.

n: 应该 means "should" or "ought to". Its negative is 不应该. It goes right before the verb.

x.en: You should go to bed earlier.

t: Two actions at once with 一边
p: 一边 A 一边 B
n: Put 一边 before each of two verbs to show that one person is doing both at the same time.

x.h: 他一边吃饭一边看电视。
x.py: Tā yìbiān chīfàn yìbiān kàn diànshì.

x.h: 我一边听音乐，一边做作业。
x.py: Wǒ yìbiān tīng yīnyuè, yìbiān zuò zuòyè.
x.en: I do homework while listening to music.

n: 只有 gives the only condition under which B can happen, and 才 goes before the verb of the result: "only if A, then B".

x.en: Only by working hard can you succeed.

x.h: 只有多练习，才能说好汉语。
x.py: Zhǐyǒu duō liànxí, cái néng shuō hǎo hànyǔ.
x.en: Only with lots of practice can you speak Chinese well.

x.py: Zhǐyǒu nǐ cái néng bāng wǒ.

n: 不但 means "not only" and 而且 means "but also". The second part adds something to the first.

x.h: 他不但会说汉语，而且说得很好。
x.py: Tā bùdàn huì shuō hànyǔ, érqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
x.en: He can not only speak Chinese, but speaks it well.

x.h: 这个地方不但漂亮，而且很安静。
x.py: Zhè gè dìfang bùdàn piàoliang, érqiě hěn ānjìng.
x.en: This place is not only pretty but also quiet.

x.h: 她不但聪明，而且很努力。
x.py: Tā bùdàn cōngming, érqiě hěn nǔlì.
x.en: She is not only smart but also hardworking.

n: 是...的 puts the focus on how, when, where or by whom a past event happened. The event itself is already known.

x.en: It was yesterday that I came.

x.py: Tā shì zuò fēijī lái de.
Nǐ shì zài nǎr mǎi de?

n: A second word after the verb tells the result of the action: 完 (finished), 懂 (understood), 见 (perceived), 到 (reached). The negative uses 没.

x.py: Nǐ shuō shénme? Wǒ méi tīng dǒng.
x.en: What did you say? I didn't understand.

x.py: Nǐ kàn jiàn wǒ de shǒujī le ma?

n: Doubling a verb makes the action short, light or tentative: "have a little ..." It is often used in suggestions and requests. The second copy is usually in neutral tone.

x.py: Wǒ xiǎng xiang, zài gàosu nǐ.
x.en: Let me think, then I'll tell you.

n: 把 moves the object in front of the verb to show what you do to it. The verb must be followed by a result, a place or 了; a bare verb is not enough.

x.py: Wǒ bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
x.en: I put the book on the table.

x.py: Tā bǎ zuòyè zuò wán le.

n: 被 marks the doer of an action done to the subject: "was ...ed by". The doer can be dropped. In speech 让 and 叫 are also used.

x.h: 我的手机被弟弟拿走了。
x.py: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi dìdi ná zǒu le.
x.en: My phone was taken away by my younger brother.

x.py: Bēizi bèi tā dǎ pò le.
x.en: The cup was broken by him.
He was criticised by the teacher.

n: 起来 after a verb or adjective can mean "to begin" (笑起来 = burst out laughing) or "when you look at / try it" (看起来, 听起来).

x.py: Zhè gè cài kàn qǐlái hěn hǎochī.

t: Doing it in a certain way with 地
n: 地 attaches a description to a verb to say how an action is done. It is written 地 but sounds like 的 and 得.
必须 means "must" and is stronger than 应该. Its negative is 不用 or 不必 ("need not"), not 不必须.

x.py: Wǒmen bìxū qī diǎn dào xuéxiào.
x.en: We must be at school by seven.

n: 或者 means "or" in statements and suggestions. In a question that offers a choice, use 还是 instead.

x.py: Nǐ kěyǐ hē chá huòzhě kāfēi.
x.en: You can have tea or coffee.

x.h: 星期六或者星期天我都有时间。
x.py: Xīngqīliù huòzhě xīngqītiān wǒ dōu yǒu shíjiān.
x.en: I am free on Saturday or Sunday.

x.py: Wǒ xiǎng chī miàntiáo huòzhě mǐfàn.
x.en: I want to eat noodles or rice.

n: 关于 introduces the topic that something is about. The phrase goes before the noun it describes (with 的) or at the start of the sentence.

x.py: Zhè shì guānyú Zhōngguó de shū.
x.en: This is a book about China.

x.h: 关于这个问题，我不知道。
x.py: Guānyú zhè gè wèntí, wǒ bù zhīdao.
x.en: About this question, I don't know.

x.h: 他写了一本关于北京的书。
x.py: Tā xiě le yì běn guānyú Běijīng de shū.
x.en: He wrote a book about Beijing.

n: 其实 introduces what is actually true, often against what you might expect or what someone just said.

x.h: 他看起来很年轻，其实已经四十岁了。
x.py: Tā kàn qǐlái hěn niánqīng, qíshí yǐjīng sìshí suì le.
x.en: He looks young, but is in fact already forty.

x.py: Qíshí wǒ bù xǐhuan chī yú.
Zhè gè wèntí qíshí hěn jiǎndān.
x.en: This question is actually very simple.

p: 除了 A 以外，B 还 / 都...
n: 除了 A 以外 followed by 都 means "except A"; followed by 还 or 也 it means "besides A, there is also B".

x.h: 除了我以外，大家都来了。
x.py: Chúle wǒ yǐwài, dàjiā dōu lái le.

x.h: 除了中文以外，他还会说英语。
x.py: Chúle zhōngwén yǐwài, tā hái huì shuō yīngyǔ.
x.en: Besides Chinese, he also speaks English.

x.h: 除了周末，我每天都工作。
x.py: Chúle zhōumò, wǒ měitiān dōu gōngzuò.
x.en: Except for weekends, I work every day.

n: 越...越... means "the more ... the more ...". 越来越 + adjective means "more and more".

x.py: Tiānqì yuè lái yuè lěng le.
x.en: The weather is getting colder and colder.

x.py: Nǐ yuè liànxí, yuè huì shuō.
x.en: The more you practise, the better you speak.
The more we chat, the happier we get.

n: 终于 means "finally", after a long wait or lots of effort. It carries a feeling of relief and usually goes with 了.

x.h: 我终于找到了我的手机。
x.py: Wǒ zhōngyú zhǎo dào le wǒ de shǒujī.

n: 比较 before an adjective or a verb of feeling means "fairly" or "relatively". It is milder than 很.
几乎 means "almost" or "nearly". With a negative it means "hardly any".

x.py: Wǒ jīhū měitiān dōu qù gōngyuán.
x.en: I go to the park almost every day.
There is almost nobody in the classroom.

n: 根据 introduces the source or evidence behind a statement: "according to / based on".

x.h: 根据天气预报，明天会下雨。
x.py: Gēnjù tiānqì yùbào, míngtiān huì xiàyǔ.
x.en: According to the weather forecast, it will rain tomorrow.

x.h: 根据老师说的，明天考试。
x.py: Gēnjù lǎoshī shuō de, míngtiān kǎoshì.
x.en: According to the teacher, there is an exam tomorrow.
According to the map, the bank is on the left.

n: 向 means "towards" for directions, or "from / to" for a person you learn from or ask something of: 向他学习, 向左走.

x.en: I want to learn from him.

n: 对 introduces the topic and 感兴趣 means "be interested in". To intensify, put 很 or 非常 before 感兴趣.

x.en: He is very interested in history.

p: 连 + noun + 都 / 也 + verb
n: 连...都... means "even". It stresses an extreme example to show that everything else is also true (or, with a negative, not true).

x.py: Tā lián fàn dōu méi chī.

x.h: 我连他的名字都不知道。
x.py: Wǒ lián tā de míngzi dōu bù zhīdao.
x.en: I don't even know his name.

t: Can / cannot: 得 and 不
n: Put 得 (can) or 不 (cannot) between a verb and its result word. 听得懂 means "can understand by listening" and 听不懂 means "cannot".

x.py: Wǒ tīng de dǒng tā shuō de huà.
x.en: I can understand what he says.

x.py: Tā shuō de tài kuài, wǒ tīng bù dǒng.
x.en: He speaks too fast, I can't understand.

x.py: Zhème duō cài, wǒ chī bù wán.
x.en: There is so much food, I can't finish it.
